pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis (secondary to an ovarian teratoma) THE SMOKING GUN: The combination of acute psychosis, severe choreoathetoid dyskinesias, extreme delta brush pattern on EEG, and a complex ovarian mass (mature cystic teratoma containing ectopic neural tissue). PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The patient has a mature cystic ovarian teratoma containing ectopic neural tissue that expresses GluN1 subunits of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors. The immune system recognizes these neuronal antigens as foreign and mounts an autoantibody response (IgG against GluN1). These autoantibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and cause selective cross-linking and internalisation of NMDA receptors on presynaptic GABAergic interneurons. This leads to severe disinhibition of forebrain neuronal networks and brainstem structures, resulting in a classic sequence: flu-like prodrome, acute psychiatric symptoms, movement disorders, coma, autonomic instability, and central hypoventilation.
